For the family matinee strand the club started in 2025 (Saturdays, 11am, kids free, adults £3). Which studios to pull from, and what I keep mixing up.

## Studio Ghibli

Founded 1985, Koganei, Tokyo. Miyazaki and Takahata. Screened "My Neighbour Totoro" (1988) on 8 March 2025, 52 people, 31 of them under 12. Dubbed version for the matinee, subtitled at 2pm for the grown-ups. GKIDS handles the UK licences now, ref GK-UK-2025-118, £95.

## Aardman

Bristol. Plasticine, Nick Park. "The Wrong Trousers" (1993) is 30 minutes and perfect, the train chase is better editing than most action films. Paired it with "A Grand Day Out" (1989) on 12 April 2025.

## Cartoon Saloon

Kilkenny, Ireland. Tomm Moore. "Song of the Sea" (2014) and "Wolfwalkers" (2020). Hand-drawn, flat, Celtic knotwork everywhere. Ishbel cried at "Song of the Sea". Licence was the dearest of the strand at £140.

## Laika and the odd ones

Laika in Portland, stop-motion, "Coraline" (2009), too scary for the under-8s, we found out the hard way. And "Flow" (2024, Gints Zilbalodis), made by a tiny team in open-source Blender, no dialogue, won the Oscar, see [[Oscar predictions]]. Booked for 6 September 2025.
